newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian government on brink of collapse.
newsitem.headline: Estonian government on brink of collapse.

text.p: The coalition government of the Baltic state of Estonia was on the verge of collapse on Wednesday after six ministers from the junior government announced their resignation.

The coalition was plunged into crisis after Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi signed a co-operation deal with the leading opposition party, infuriating his coalition partners from the Reform Party and sparking the resignations.

The government, an alliance of the Coalition and Reform parties, is the sixth administration since Estonia, smallest of the three Baltic states, regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991.
The resignations were announced in an open letter to Vaehi, who still has to formally approve them.
"The open letter of the Reform Party ministers cannot be treated as their official resignation," Vaehi told journalists, implying he wanted individual notices to quit.
The Reformists set Vaehi a Wednesday afternoon deadline to scrap the deal with the opposition Centre Party but he failed to comply.

"Tomorrow the Reform Party council will decide whether the party will continue in the coalition but already today we have made the conclusion for ourselves that we cannot continue in the government led by you," the resignation letter to Vaehi said.
The Reform Party itself decides on Thursday whether to quit the government, which includes a smaller bloc of rural parties.
Reform Party leader and Foreign Minister Siim Kallas, one of the ministers to resign, said that reassurances the Centre Party would not be included in the government were insufficient.
He criticised the agreement for changing Estonia's foreign policy and bringing it closer to huge neighbour Russia, which many Estonians fear wants to reassert its influence over them.
"...in the chapter on international relations, it talks of Russia but there is not a single word on the European Union," Kallas told journalists, speaking about the co-operation pact.

Russia ruled Estonia and fellow Baltic states Latvia and Lithuania for most of the last 200 years and all three look with bitterness on the 50 years during which they lived as unwilling Soviet citizens.
Vaehi has refused to cancel the pact with the Centre Party and has tried to reassure his partners that the deal would not lead to the Centre Party joining the coalition.
Vaehi insisted that the Coalition and Centre parties would simply work together to "strengthen democracy".
The previous government was a Coalition/Centre partnership which collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have taped confidential conversations.
Estonia, deemed one of the most successful reformers in eastern Europe, has managed to keep on a steady path of reform despite frequent political turmoil.
